workflow_bottleneck: Unknown mixture of host evaluation, native compute, geometry prep, submission, GPU execution, and present latency
simplest_impl: Add lightweight native scoped spans with scenario/frame/scene/seed IDs; MAXScript timestamps around boundary calls; ETW/WPR trace; PresentMon CSV; raw JSON/CSV output; release build switch-off
simpler_alternative: Use only WPR/WPA plus external PresentMon and a few MAXScript timestamps
strongest_argument_against: Markers and synchronization probes add overhead and can perturb short frames
experiment: Run baseline and instrumented builds on fixed scenes; cold/warm; navigation/edit/rebuild/animation/render-prep; correlate spans to ETW and present intervals; validate output hash/counts
accept_reject_thresholds: Instrumentation overhead <=2% for end-to-end median and <=5% p95; no correctness/hash difference; every measured stage reconciles to wall-time critical path
reversal_condition: If host APIs cannot safely accept markers, keep external WPR/PresentMon and instrument only native kernel boundaries

option: Optimize kernel only after contribution is measured
workflow_bottleneck: Potentially small kernel share of artist-visible critical path
simplest_impl: Use Amdahl bound from measured critical-path fraction p; optimize only if p and tail latency justify it
simpler_alternative: Optimize allocation, invalidation, or marshalling first if they dominate
strongest_argument_against: Kernel micro-optimization can improve an isolated timer while leaving edit-to-visible unchanged
experiment: Paired before/after kernel build; fixed seed and correctness oracle; compare end-to-end and kernel spans across small/large/unique-source cases
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if target scenario median improves >=20% and p95 does not regress; reject if end-to-end gain <5% or small-scene latency regresses >5%
reversal_condition: Reverse if trace shows kernel >=50% of critical path across priority workloads

workflow_bottleneck: Large display/instance preparation or GPU-bound viewport
simplest_impl: Keep current CPU/Nitrous DX11 path until transfer-inclusive crossover is measured; prototype only isolated if needed
simpler_alternative: Improve Nitrous instance data, batching, culling, and CPU preparation
strongest_argument_against: Transfers, synchronization, device ownership, fallback, renderer coexistence, and DX11 host constraints add substantial complexity
experiment: Compare CPU/Nitrous baseline and GPU prototype including upload, synchronization, device loss, memory, cold/warm, and 32 GB target; exact image/count hash
accept_reject_thresholds: Do not adopt unless transfer-inclusive end-to-end median improves >=30%, p95 improves, memory bound is met, and CPU fallback is correct
reversal_condition: Reverse if large unique-source workloads show stable transfer-inclusive GPU win with supportable ownership contract

option: Use ApplicationPlugins bundle with isolated dependency policy
workflow_bottleneck: DLL collisions, wrong Max-version load, upgrade/uninstall failure
simplest_impl: Per-version package directories; precise SeriesMin/SeriesMax; stable UpgradeCode; changing ProductCode/AppVersion; module path/hash manifest; controlled dependency loading; VC++ prerequisite
simpler_alternative: Loose plugin-folder deployment for internal experiments
strongest_argument_against: Packaging and installer work costs time; old `.mzp` habits are simpler for scripts
experiment: Install clean machine with Max 2026 and 2027, both updates; upgrade/downgrade/uninstall; inspect loaded modules and hashes; run with Corona/V-Ray
accept_reject_thresholds: Zero wrong-version loads, no duplicate same-named private DLLs, clean uninstall, deterministic module manifest, no startup error
reversal_condition: Reverse only for a script-only internal tool with no native/managed binary

workflow_bottleneck: Scene reopen, save-as-old, merge/XRef, scripted redefinition, parameter compatibility
simplest_impl: Stable classIDs; explicit plugin/schema version; update conversion; chunked native data; preserve old chunks; reference-safe ownership; missing-plugin diagnostic
simpler_alternative: Freeze schema and reject all old scenes
strongest_argument_against: Schema freeze shifts cost to users and does not solve native chunk compatibility
experiment: Generate scenes in each version; load in later build; edit all parameters; save/load/merge/XRef/clone/undo/reset; compare semantic state and deterministic output hash
accept_reject_thresholds: No silent parameter loss; explicit conversion warnings where needed; semantic state and output oracle match; no crash on missing plugin
reversal_condition: Reverse only if product explicitly declares no scene compatibility and controls all files

workflow_bottleneck: Unknown behavior under scale, long sessions, animation, renderer contention, low memory, and device failure
simplest_impl: Automate small/large/unique/pathological scenes, cold/warm, 32 GB, Manual/Real-time, animation, save/load/reset/merge/clone/XRef, Undo/Redo, cancellation/shutdown, Corona/V-Ray
simpler_alternative: Manual smoke tests plus synthetic proxy FPS demo
strongest_argument_against: Automation and scene curation are expensive; broad matrix can delay beta
experiment: Run deterministic harness per stage with raw logs, image/count/hash oracle, memory/VRAM telemetry, crash/hang capture
accept_reject_thresholds: Alpha claims basic load/create/edit only; beta claims tested feature combinations; RC claims exact host/update/hardware/package matrix only; no global renderer claim
reversal_condition: Reverse scope if supported workflow is intentionally narrower and documented

option: Keep PIX out of primary DX11 timing path
workflow_bottleneck: Need GPU timing on Nitrous DX11
simplest_impl: Use WPR/WPA + PresentMon + vendor timeline; reserve PIX for D3D12 or diagnostic D3D11On12 captures
simpler_alternative: Use PIX D3D11On12 anyway
strongest_argument_against: PIX translation can alter behavior and timing captures lack ordinary D3D11 GPU work
experiment: Capture identical navigation/edit runs with PIX D3D11On12, WPR, PresentMon; compare overhead and GPU evidence
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject PIX as quantitative DX11 GPU timer if GPU work is absent/translated or overhead changes p95 >5%
reversal_condition: Reverse if current PIX release provides validated native-DX11 timing on tested Max path

workflow_bottleneck: Repeated selection of triangles from a stable area/mask distribution
simplest_impl: Keep area array plus prefix CDF and binary search; omit zero-area triangles
simpler_alternative: Direct linear scan for very small triangle counts
strongest_argument_against: Alias can reduce selection cost but adds memory, build work, and invalidation complexity
experiment: For T in {32,128,512,2048,8192}, Q in {1,10,1e3,1e6}, measure build, selection, cache misses, and output histogram; compare against a high-precision area oracle
accept_reject_thresholds: Adopt alias only if total build+Q*sample time improves by at least 20% on representative repeated workloads without changing count/histogram; otherwise keep CDF
reversal_condition: Frequent mask/topology edits or small Q reverse the choice

workflow_bottleneck: Output changes with thread schedule, retry counts, or worker partitioning
simplest_impl: Use Philox/Threefry-style counter(key,logical_id) with explicit purpose and attempt domains
simpler_alternative: One deterministic serial RNG stream
strongest_argument_against: Changing stream mapping can change historical point identities and exact output
experiment: Generate identical logical inputs with 1,2,4,8,16 threads and different task partitions; compare bitwise outputs and statistical tests
accept_reject_thresholds: Require bitwise equality if current contract demands it; otherwise require count, containment, spacing, and distribution parity with documented position tolerance
reversal_condition: If legacy sequence identity is contractual, preserve legacy mode and add keyed mode explicitly

workflow_bottleneck: Point-versus-all-point proximity checks dominate interactive scatter rebuilds
simplest_impl: Fixed-radius grid with cell width r/sqrt(3), reused arrays, squared-distance narrow phase
simpler_alternative: Direct loop for small N
strongest_argument_against: Poor for highly skewed density, variable radii, or geodesic spacing
experiment: Sweep N, radius, domain extent, density skew, and query count; measure candidate checks, build/update, p95 latency, and memory
accept_reject_thresholds: Adopt when candidate checks fall materially and total frame/rebuild time improves at least 20% without false negatives; retain direct-loop oracle
reversal_condition: Small N, highly skewed occupancy, or variable-radius semantics reverse it

workflow_bottleneck: Need blue-noise spacing on irregular/folded meshes without projection bias
simplest_impl: Uniform area sample pool, spatial cell elimination, optional exact-count elimination
simpler_alternative: World-space Bridson dart throwing with narrow-phase mesh checks
strongest_argument_against: Oversampling and elimination consume memory and may not guarantee maximal coverage
experiment: For plane, thin shell, folded mesh, holes, and mixed triangle scales, compare power spectrum/nearest-neighbor distribution, count, build time, and boundary bias
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if surface distribution and spacing improve at an agreed quality target with bounded memory; otherwise use simpler darts
reversal_condition: If visual quality is indistinguishable or mesh edits dominate, reject

workflow_bottleneck: Closest-point/ray/collision candidate enumeration across many triangles
simplest_impl: Use existing/simple BVH or grid only after measuring; rebuild/refit policy explicit
simpler_alternative: Direct triangle loop as oracle and small-workload path
strongest_argument_against: Index build/invalidation may cost more than queries; external dependency adds maintenance
experiment: For actual mesh sizes and edit patterns, measure build, refit, rebuild, Q-query latency, candidate count, memory, and worst cases with skew/degenerate triangles
accept_reject_thresholds: Select by total time: build+Q*query; require no missed candidates against brute-force oracle and at least 20% total improvement
reversal_condition: Small Q, frequent topology edits, or similar total time favors direct/grid

workflow_bottleneck: Near-boundary and near-degenerate containment/orientation decisions are unstable
simplest_impl: Fast filtered predicate with Shewchuk-style adaptive fallback for sign decisions
simpler_alternative: Fixed epsilon around ordinary floating-point tests
strongest_argument_against: Fallback code complexity and integration/ABI review cost
experiment: Generate adversarial near-collinear, large-coordinate, mirrored, and boundary-on-edge cases; compare sign against exact/integer oracle where available
accept_reject_thresholds: Zero false classifications in adversarial corpus; measure fallback rate and ensure normal workloads incur acceptable overhead
reversal_condition: If inputs are formally bounded and no failures occur, keep simpler filter but retain tests

workflow_bottleneck: FMA/reassociation/thread reductions alter selected points or counts
simplest_impl: Keep decision-critical code under /fp:precise or stricter local controls; use fixed reduction order
simpler_alternative: Global /fp:fast for all native code
strongest_argument_against: May reduce peak arithmetic throughput and differ from legacy output
experiment: Compile same corpus with /fp:precise, /fp:precise+/fp:contract, /fp:fast; vary ISA and thread count; compare output and performance
accept_reject_thresholds: Do not change flags solely for speed; require no contract-visible output change or obtain explicit approval for a changed contract
reversal_condition: If decisions are tolerance-based and parity is not contractual, use faster mode outside predicates/reductions

workflow_bottleneck: Hot loops spend time on memory traffic and allocation rather than arithmetic
simplest_impl: Reuse owned scratch buffers and use SoA for large homogeneous scans
simpler_alternative: Retain current AoS and allocator behavior
strongest_argument_against: Layout conversion and lifetime bugs can outweigh gains for small workloads
experiment: Profile cache misses, allocation count, vectorization reports, and end-to-end time for small/medium/large N
accept_reject_thresholds: Adopt only if end-to-end time improves at least 10% with no memory growth beyond target and no reproducibility change
reversal_condition: If arithmetic/indexing dominates or N is small, retain AoS

workflow_bottleneck: Host ABI/SDK compatibility and deployment validation
simplest_impl: Build and load-test one binary per supported Max SDK/API target
simpler_alternative: Assume cross-version loading
strongest_argument_against: Autodesk documentation identifies incompatibility between these releases
experiment: Build minimal plug-in against each installed SDK; load, scatter, edit, save, and render smoke tests in both hosts
accept_reject_thresholds: Require successful load and behavioral smoke tests in every supported host; no cross-loading assumption
reversal_condition: Only if Autodesk provides an explicit compatibility guarantee for the exact SDK pair

option: Keep serial optimized computation as the baseline
workflow_bottleneck: Unknown until local profiling; likely small scatter rebuilds or host-evaluation-dominated work
simplest_impl: Optimize allocations, data layout, culling, and deterministic loops; retain a serial path
simpler_alternative: No new concurrency infrastructure
strongest_argument_against: May leave large owned-data workloads slower than necessary
experiment: Fixed snapshots at small/medium/large counts; compare serial wall time, p95 main-thread stall, allocations, and output hash/tolerance
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept as default if parallel speedup is <1.2x on large input or worsens p95 latency >10%; reject only if bounded parallel is >=1.2x faster with no correctness or latency regression
reversal_condition: Measured large owned-data workloads show durable speedup and acceptable latency

option: Bounded synchronous fork/join over owned arrays
workflow_bottleneck: CPU-heavy independent placement/analysis after a main-thread snapshot
simplest_impl: One parallel range, fixed worker cap, minimum-work cutoff, per-range outputs, deterministic merge, join before publish
simpler_alternative: Serial optimized implementation
strongest_argument_against: Fork/join overhead, renderer contention, and cache pressure can erase gains
experiment: For identical immutable snapshots and seeds, run serial and worker caps 1/2/half/all-allowed across grain sizes; collect wall time, p50/p95/p99 interaction stall, CPU, memory, and exact/tolerance parity
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept if zero crashes/hangs, zero unacceptable parity failures, large-case wall time improves >=20%, and p95 interaction latency is no worse than baseline; reject if <10% gain or p95 worsens >10%
reversal_condition: Results show gains only under a persistent executor or a different owned-data partition

workflow_bottleneck: Repeated long asynchronous rebuilds where startup cost is material
simplest_impl: Only after profiling; executor owns no Max objects, supports cancellation, and drains and joins before unload
simpler_alternative: Synchronous bounded fork/join
strongest_argument_against: Highest lifetime/shutdown complexity and stale-result risk
experiment: Stress repeated rebuilds while changing parameters, undo/redo, deleting nodes, loading/resetting scenes, closing Max, and unloading/reloading plugin; monitor hangs, use-after-free, stale publications, and teardown time
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject unless synchronous execution misses a defined responsiveness target and persistent executor has zero lifecycle failures over an extended stress run; stop on first unload/scene-lifecycle fault
reversal_condition: Measured startup cost is a dominant fraction of a long-lived workload and lifecycle stress passes

workflow_bottleneck: Long native compute that blocks interaction but does not require host access during compute
simplest_impl: Main-thread snapshot plus generation/cancellation token; worker computes only owned data; PostTask publishes only if generation and host validity still match
simpler_alternative: Event coalescing plus synchronous rebuild
strongest_argument_against: More stale work, memory retention, cancellation, and undo/redo complexity
experiment: Rapid parameter edits, undo/redo, scene reset/load, node deletion, render start/stop, and shutdown while workers run; verify stale results never publish and all workers stop before unload
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if interaction p95 improves materially (proposed >=20%) with zero stale publications/crashes; reject if snapshot or queue overhead dominates or stale-result handling is ambiguous
reversal_condition: Work is short enough for coalesced synchronous rebuild or host evaluation dominates

workflow_bottleneck: Worker completion must mutate Max UI/scene/plugin host state
simplest_impl: Post a MainThreadTask carrying an owned result and generation token; Execute validates state and applies on main thread
simpler_alternative: Main-thread timer/event coalescing for simple scripts
strongest_argument_against: Queue timing and shutdown semantics require validation; task payload can outlive plugin state
experiment: Post tasks while resetting/loading/closing Max; confirm Execute occurs on main thread, stale tasks are discarded, and task payloads do not retain unloaded code
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept when lifecycle stress shows zero callback-after-unload and zero stale publication; fallback to simple coalescing if queue integration is unavailable in target SDK
reversal_condition: Target host build does not pump tasks reliably or task manager is unavailable

workflow_bottleneck: Need bounded native ranges and Max already loads TBB
simplest_impl: Use exact SDK-supported TBB headers/runtime only after dependency audit; cap via arena/Max controls where documented; otherwise use standard bounded implementation
simpler_alternative: std::thread or PPL with explicit fixed worker count
strongest_argument_against: Bundled-version/ABI/DLL conflicts and no general plugin-pool guarantee
experiment: Inspect loaded DLLs and link dependencies in clean Max 2026/2027 installs; benchmark TBB versus serial and a private bounded implementation under idle and renderer-active states
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if exact runtime loads cleanly on both host versions, no DLL collision, and it wins the same parity/latency thresholds as DX-CC-02; reject on unresolved deployment ambiguity
reversal_condition: Autodesk publishes a supported plugin executor or local profiling shows no TBB benefit

workflow_bottleneck: CPU-heavy plugin rebuilds concurrent with Corona/V-Ray final or interactive rendering
simplest_impl: Run fixed plugin worker caps against renderer default/all-core and renderer-limited modes; expose conservative cap or disable background compute during final render
simpler_alternative: Pause/coalesce plugin work during rendering
strongest_argument_against: Any cap can reduce either render throughput or rebuild throughput
experiment: Fixed scene and render settings; compare renderer-only, plugin-only, and concurrent runs; record render wall time, plugin wall time, UI p95/p99, cancellation latency, CPU package power/thermal state, and peak memory
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if concurrent render time and UI latency remain within agreed budgets (proposed <=5% render regression and <=10% UI p95 regression); otherwise serialize/coalesce
reversal_condition: Target workflows never overlap plugin work and rendering

workflow_bottleneck: P/E placement, SMT contention, or NUMA locality causes latency variance
simplest_impl: Let Windows/Thread Director schedule by default; test oneTBB constraints only after evidence
simpler_alternative: No affinity or core-type policy
strongest_argument_against: Hard pinning can harm portability and defeat OS scheduling; NUMA locality may conflict with renderer
experiment: On target P/E and NUMA systems, compare default scheduling, worker caps, SMT-off/one-thread-per-core variant, and measured task_arena constraints; collect wall and tail latency
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject manual pinning unless it improves p95/p99 and wall time consistently across repeated runs without harming renderer; accept default OS scheduling when variance is within budget
reversal_condition: Repeated profiling shows stable, large gains from a specific topology constraint

workflow_bottleneck: CPU expansion and repeated submission of identical source triangles during navigation/animation
simplest_impl: Implement one IObjectDisplay2 path with one retained source geometry per compatible batch, InstanceDisplayGeometry, pMatrices, CreateInstanceData on topology/count changes, UpdateInstanceData on transform-only changes, and CPU fallback
simpler_alternative: Keep current CPU-batched path and first optimize rebuild invalidation/batching
strongest_argument_against: GPU path adds SDK integration, stream requirements, resource lifetime, device-reset, and per-instance interaction complexity
experiment: Use identical source meshes, instance transforms, counts, viewport size, driver, Standard/High Quality modes, and camera path. Compare current CPU batch against retained render-item/viewport-instancing prototype. Record median/p95 synchronous redraw duration, presentation FPS, CPU build/upload time, GPU memory, system RAM, and visible-output checksum/image diff.
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only if prototype improves p95 redraw time or sustained interactive frame delivery by a predefined margin (suggest 25%) without correctness regressions, unbounded VRAM growth, or failed rebuild/device tests. Reject if gains are below measurement noise or only appear in uncontrolled FPS overlay.
confidence: high that API is viable; unknown benefit until measured
reversal_condition: If CPU batching matches or beats it on target workloads, or if required selection/material/driver behavior cannot be preserved, keep CPU path.

option: Keep CPU batching as long-term baseline/fallback
workflow_bottleneck: Unsupported drivers, incompatible material/UVW overrides, topology-changing/deforming sources, and easier selection/hit testing
simplest_impl: Retain source-side CPU batching, but group by source/material and avoid rebuilds when transforms only change
simpler_alternative: Use only point/box previews and disable full display
strongest_argument_against: CPU expansion can become the dominant cost at high counts and may duplicate memory
experiment: Run current CPU path with source-vertex counts and instance counts swept independently; compare expanded CPU memory and redraw time to budgeted target on 32 GB workstation.
accept_reject_thresholds: Keep as mandatory fallback regardless of GPU result. Reject only if it prevents required interactive workload even after display budgets/proxies are applied.
reversal_condition: If target workloads show CPU path is consistently unacceptable and GPU path passes all lifecycle/correctness tests.

option: Explicit representation ladder and display budgets
workflow_bottleneck: Full meshes overload rasterization and GPU memory even when scattering computation is fast
simplest_impl: Implement None/Dot/Box/WireBox/PointCloud/Proxy/Full, plus max instances and max polygons; optionally adaptive full-to-box while actively navigating
simpler_alternative: Single fixed proxy mode
strongest_argument_against: Reduced display fidelity may surprise users and must be decoupled from render counts
experiment: For fixed scatter state, sweep representations and budgets while measuring interaction latency and checking silhouette/selection expectations. Verify viewport count can differ from render count.
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept if every representation has deterministic limits, no viewport budget changes render output, and active navigation remains within agreed p95 latency. Reject only representations that cannot meet correctness or maintenance requirements.
reversal_condition: If source geometry is always small enough that full display meets target latency.

option: Separate viewport culling/LOD from render-time instance data
workflow_bottleneck: Viewport optimization can omit instances needed by reflections, shadows, motion blur, or off-camera rays
simplest_impl: Maintain independent viewport display subset and renderer-facing full instance source; expose camera clipping only as explicit viewport/scene-parse optimization with warning
simpler_alternative: Do not cull; always display/render all instances
strongest_argument_against: Separate sets increase state and invalidation complexity
experiment: Render a camera-framed scene with off-camera instances contributing to reflection/shadow; compare with viewport-culling subset. Verify renderer instance data is unaffected by viewport budget/culling.
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject any implementation where viewport culling changes final render semantics. Accept camera clipping only with documented extend-view behavior and renderer-specific tests.
reversal_condition: Only if product explicitly accepts altered render semantics, which current requirements do not support.

workflow_bottleneck: Final-render duplication and renderer-specific instance handling
simplest_impl: Implement only after confirming target renderer support and defining source/target/motion-blur/material override contracts
simpler_alternative: Use existing aggregate GetRenderMesh/render path
strongest_argument_against: Renderer support is not guaranteed by Autodesk API; implementation may not benefit unsupported renderers
experiment: For each target renderer/version, render a source/instance scene with transforms, motion blur, material/MatID/UVW overrides, reflections, and shadows. Compare render output and memory/time against existing path.
accept_reject_thresholds: Do not accept on API existence alone. Accept per renderer only when output matches and render memory/time improves on representative workloads; otherwise retain aggregate fallback.
reversal_condition: Renderer vendors document and pass support tests, or current rendering is proven bottleneck.

workflow_bottleneck: Need for specialized draw behavior beyond standard geometry/instancing
simplest_impl: Only use if standard GeometryRenderItemHandle/InstanceDisplayGeometry cannot express required behavior; keep Realize/Display self-contained
simpler_alternative: Use standard InstanceDisplayGeometry and legacy fallback
strongest_argument_against: Custom path has highest threading/resource-lifetime complexity
experiment: Stress multiple viewports, repeated redraws, node hide/unhide, driver/device changes, plugin unload, and source invalidation while checking for stale handles/crashes.
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject unless standard API cannot implement a required feature and custom path passes lifecycle stress tests with measurable benefit.
reversal_condition: A required display feature cannot be represented with standard retained geometry/instancing.

workflow_bottleneck: Unknown candidate-generation, mask, closest-point, spacing, extraction, or publication share
simplest_impl: Instrument edit-to-visible path; improve packed data, SIMD, spatial indexing, bounded worker ownership, and invalidation contracts
simpler_alternative: Keep current implementation until profiling identifies a hot path
strongest_argument_against: May leave a genuinely dominant dense kernel unaccelerated
experiment: Three scenes; measure extraction, CPU kernels, publication, and viewport redraw separately; record median/p95
accept_reject_thresholds: Proceed with CPU work by default; stop GPU proposal if candidate share <20% or ideal Amdahl ceiling <=1.25x
reversal_condition: Measured GPU-worthy kernel dominates and CPU optimization plateaus

workflow_bottleneck: Large dense candidate generation or mask evaluation with regular data
simplest_impl: Compile one HLSL CS 5.x kernel; private D3D11 buffers; batch upload; dispatch; read back compact result; CPU publication
simpler_alternative: Optimized CPU implementation
strongest_argument_against: No documented Autodesk Nitrous compute-dispatch or arbitrary buffer-sharing contract; GPU may contend with viewport
experiment: Implement one kernel and compare transfer-inclusive edit-to-visible latency against CPU; validate candidate IDs/positions
accept_reject_thresholds: Accept only >=1.5x median speedup, <=10% p95 regression, and declared correctness tolerance; reject below 1.25x
reversal_condition: Autodesk documents supported compute/interop path or local measurements show no transfer penalty

workflow_bottleneck: Same as DX11, but only for NVIDIA users and CUDA-capable machines
simplest_impl: Private CUDA allocations; persistent buffers; pinned staging; one batched kernel; CPU fallback; explicit device selection
simpler_alternative: DirectCompute/D3D11 or optimized CPU
strongest_argument_against: NVIDIA-only; driver/runtime packaging; V-Ray GPU/Vantage contention; D3D11 interop lifecycle risk
experiment: Run CUDA prototype on at least two NVIDIA generations and one renderer-active case; measure H2D/kernel/D2H/sync separately
accept_reject_thresholds: Require same end-to-end thresholds as DX11 plus no unacceptable renderer/UI contention and a supported fallback
reversal_condition: NVIDIA is a contractual target and measured speedup remains after renderer contention

workflow_bottleneck: Cross-vendor dense kernels where NVIDIA/AMD/Intel coverage is a hard requirement
simplest_impl: Only consider after feature-query matrix and target-driver qualification; use basic kernels without optional features
simpler_alternative: CPU baseline or D3D11 on Windows
strongest_argument_against: OpenCL 3.x optional features, driver/extension variance, AMD Windows coverage uncertainty, testing burden
experiment: Enumerate required extensions/features on representative NVIDIA/AMD/Intel Windows systems; run same kernel and correctness suite
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject first-backend work unless at least 90% of target machines pass required feature/correctness tests and transfer-inclusive speedup meets 1.5x
reversal_condition: User telemetry proves broad non-NVIDIA demand and a stable supported feature subset

workflow_bottleneck: Multi-architecture portability after one kernel has proven valuable
classification: reject as first backend; investigate later
simplest_impl: Prototype only after a backend-specific win; target a narrowly defined kernel and fixed toolchain
simpler_alternative: DirectCompute/D3D11 or CUDA plus CPU fallback
strongest_argument_against: Compiler/runtime/plugin deployment and debugging cost arrives before proven benefit
experiment: Port the already-validated kernel; compare build/runtime packaging, correctness, and speed across target vendors
accept_reject_thresholds: Proceed only if it materially reduces maintained backend count and preserves >=1.5x end-to-end speedup
reversal_condition: Product explicitly commits to cross-vendor GPU support

workflow_bottleneck: Potential future cross-vendor compute independent of Nitrous
simplest_impl: No implementation until a supported Max/Nitrous resource and device-lifecycle path is established
simpler_alternative: DirectCompute/D3D11 or CPU
strongest_argument_against: No verified Autodesk Vulkan compute/interop path in reviewed SDK material; adds explicit synchronization/deployment complexity
experiment: Architecture spike only; no production code; document device/resource sharing and publication path
accept_reject_thresholds: Reject if it requires private device plus full copies and cannot beat D3D11/CPU transfer-inclusive latency
reversal_condition: Autodesk documents Vulkan resource/compute integration or product broadens beyond Max/Windows

workflow_bottleneck: Whether candidate kernel dominates edit-to-visible latency
simplest_impl: Instrument three representative scenes; prototype one dense kernel with private buffers; compare complete latency and correctness
simpler_alternative: Keep CPU and stop GPU work
strongest_argument_against: Kernel-only speedup can hide extraction, transfers, synchronization, readback, and publication
experiment: Measure T_extract, T_pack, T_upload, T_alloc, T_dispatch, T_kernel, T_sync, T_readback, T_publish; median/p95; repeatability; renderer-on/off
accept_reject_thresholds: Stop if p<20%, ideal Amdahl bound<=1.25x, or GPU end-to-end<1.25x; continue only at >=1.5x median, <=10% p95 regression, acceptable correctness
reversal_condition: Local data shows persistent residency and a dominant regular kernel
